findings.title: Callback invocation reads mutable function.call after registration
relevantCode: load.call(provider, ref as unknown as AssetRef<T>, context)
findings.contract: register fixes provider callbacks at registration time.
findings.reproduction: callback-capture-counterexample.mjs: register ordinary load/dispose functions; define their own call properties after registration while preserving function identity; acquire and release through @egret/engine.
findings.effect: The registered loader and disposer are never invoked, so postregistration mutation can silently replace resource behavior and skip cleanup.
findings.rationale: This changes only user-owned properties on registered callback objects and does not patch global intrinsics.
findings.recommendation: Invoke captured callables through an intrinsic invocation operation and preserve provider receiver binding. Add a narrow regression for loader/disposer own call property mutation.

resolution.code: Reflect.apply invokes captured callables with their original provider receiver; registered callable own .call properties are no longer read.
shippedRegressions: captured loader ignores a later own call property while retaining its provider receiver
captured disposer ignores a later own call property while retaining its provider receiver
resolution.redEvidence: callback-capture-red.json records the independently observed pre-fix failure. Production regression RED/GREEN logs are separately retained by the implementation run.

reviewLimits: Passing finite behavioral checks does not establish global correctness or originality.
No competitor implementation or prior probe implementation was read or copied.

Initial missing-API RED is not evidence that every specific lifecycle mechanism independently failed before implementation.
The callback-capture mismatch has an independently observed RED and final GREEN reproduction; the reviewed intrinsic invocation and two shipped regressions close AR1 within this scope.
